domains.title: Claude Code Configuration & Workflows
domains.summary: How you configure Claude Code for a team: memory files (CLAUDE.md), commands and skills, path-specific rules, hooks, plan mode, iterative refinement, and CI/CD use.

taskStatements.title: CLAUDE.md Hierarchy, Scoping, and Modular Organization
concept: CLAUDE.md files hold persistent instructions that Claude Code loads automatically at session start.

Modular organization: use @import (@docs/testing-standards.md) to keep the main file short; put topic files in .claude/rules/ (testing.md, api-conventions.md); use /memory to see which memory files are loaded.

table.title: CLAUDE.md levels
rows: Everyone, when working in that folder

steps: Diagnose 'a teammate does not get the instructions': run /memory on the teammate's machine and list loaded files.
Check where the instruction lives. In ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md = only the author gets it.
Move it to the project-level CLAUDE.md (or an imported file).
Commit to version control.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Works for me but not for new team members' -> instruction is at USER level. Move it to PROJECT level.

taskStatements.title: Custom Slash Commands and Skills
concept: A skill loads ON DEMAND (when invoked or relevant). CLAUDE.md is ALWAYS loaded. Universal standards -> CLAUDE.md. Task-specific workflows -> skills.

table.title: Where things live
rows: Personal (use a different name for a personal variant of a team skill)

table2.title: SKILL.md frontmatter
rows: Runs the skill in an isolated sub-agent context; only the result returns
Skill produces verbose output that would pollute main conversation
Restricts the tools the skill may use
Prevent destructive actions (allow only Read, Grep, Glob; omit Bash)
Shows the user which parameters to provide
Skill needs input (file path, ticket ID)

steps: Create .claude/skills/review/SKILL.md.
Add frontmatter: name, description, context: fork, allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, argument-hint.
Write the instructions (criteria, output format).
Commit the folder. The team invokes it with /review.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Skill output fills main context' -> context: fork. 'Skill must not modify files' -> allowed-tools. 'Command for whole team' -> project .claude/ folder, not ~/.claude/.

taskStatements.title: Path-Specific Rules for Conditional Convention Loading
concept: A rule file in .claude/rules/ can have YAML frontmatter with a paths: field. The rule loads ONLY when Claude works on matching files, saving context.
Files of one type spread across many folders (tests next to source) -> path-specific rule with a glob. All files in one folder (terraform/) -> directory CLAUDE.md also works.
steps: Create .claude/rules/testing.md.
Add frontmatter paths: ["**/*.test.tsx"].
Write the conventions (fixtures, naming, mocks).
Commit. The rule loads only when a test file is edited.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Conventions for files scattered across the codebase' -> .claude/rules/ + paths: glob. NOT a CLAUDE.md in every folder.

taskStatements.title: Plan Mode vs Direct Execution
taskStatements.oneLine: Plan for big / multi-file / many options. Direct for small and clear.
concept: Plan mode: large or multi-file changes (library migration across 45+ files), several valid approaches, architectural decisions, need to explore first.
Direct execution: small well-scoped change, one clear approach, single-file bug fix with a clear stack trace, one validation conditional.
The Explore subagent runs verbose discovery in its own context and returns a summary.
steps: Large migration: enter plan mode (Claude reads but does not change code).
Use the Explore subagent for wide discovery; get a summary.
Review and approve the plan.
Switch to direct execution to implement.
taskStatements.examTip: Plan mode is NOT for every task. A one-line bug fix in plan mode wastes time. Best answer often COMBINES plan mode (investigate) + direct execution (implement).

taskStatements.title: Iterative Refinement Techniques
taskStatements.oneLine: Concrete examples, tests first, interview pattern.

table.title: Techniques
rows: Give 2-3 examples of input and expected output
Write tests first, run them, share failures, repeat
Ask Claude to ask YOU questions first (cache invalidation, failure modes, edge cases)
Fix one, verify, then the next

taskStatements.examTip: 'Output format keeps varying despite detailed description' -> concrete examples. 'Developer new to the domain' -> interview pattern.

taskStatements.title: CI/CD Integration
concept: claude -p '<prompt>' runs non-interactively. Without -p the CI job hangs waiting for input.
--output-format json with --json-schema gives machine-parseable output your script turns into inline PR comments.
CLAUDE.md gives CI context: testing standards, fixture conventions, review criteria.
Session context isolation: the session that wrote the code is bad at reviewing it. Use an INDEPENDENT instance.
On re-runs after new commits: include prior review findings; report only NEW or STILL-UNADDRESSED issues.
For test generation: give existing test files so Claude does not suggest duplicates.
steps: Trigger the job on PR open or new commit.
Run claude -p "Review this diff" --output-format json --json-schema review.json.
Provide context: CLAUDE.md review criteria, prior findings, existing tests.
Use a fresh, independent instance (not the generating session).
Parse the JSON; post inline comments for new or open issues only.
taskStatements.examTip: 'CI job hangs' -> missing -p. 'Cannot parse output' -> --output-format json + --json-schema. 'Same comments repeated each commit' -> pass prior findings. 'Self-review misses bugs' -> independent instance.

testObjectives.text: Implement PostToolUse hooks that automatically enforce code quality constraints - such as formatting, linting, or test execution - after every file edit, independent of model instruction-following.
keyPoints: 'Always run Prettier' in CLAUDE.md is only a request; a hook is automatic
PostToolUse hook, matcher 'Edit|Write', type 'command', in project .claude/settings.json
Hook gets JSON on stdin including tool_input.file_path
On failure script exits with code 2 and writes to stderr; Claude Code feeds the message to Claude
Key phrase: 'independent of model instruction-following' or 'after every edit' -> hook
Events: PreToolUse (block dangerous commands), PostToolUse (format/lint/test), UserPromptSubmit, Stop (final checks), SessionStart

testObjectives.text: Distinguish instructions that must be enforced through settings permissions or hooks from those appropriately placed in CLAUDE.md, and restructure configurations accordingly.
keyPoints: Never read .env -> permissions.deny: ["Read(./.env)"]
Never run rm -rf -> permissions.deny or PreToolUse hook
Format after every edit -> PostToolUse hook
2-space indentation, prefer functional components -> CLAUDE.md
Run npm test without asking -> permissions.allow: ["Bash(npm run test *)"]
Rule: must happen / must never happen -> permissions or hooks; preference/convention -> CLAUDE.md

testObjectives.text: Select the correct Claude Code configuration mechanism - CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/ with glob patterns, Skills, hooks, or settings permissions - based on guidance type and when it should apply.
keyPoints: CLAUDE.md: guidance, always
rules + paths glob: guidance, only when matching files touched
Skill: workflow, on demand
Hook: deterministic automation on lifecycle events
Settings permissions: enforcement on every tool call (allow/ask/deny)

testObjectives.text: Select the appropriate method for providing project context to Claude Code - @ references, CLAUDE.md, or inline description - based on reusability, specificity, and cross-session need.
keyPoints: @ reference: one specific file for this task
CLAUDE.md (or @import): reused across sessions and people
Inline description: short one-off detail

testObjectives.text: Create and deploy custom slash commands in the correct project or user directory so they are available to intended users and invoked on demand for task-specific workflows.
keyPoints: Team command -> .claude/commands/<name>.md (commit it)
Personal command -> ~/.claude/commands/<name>.md
Invoke with /<name>; skills in .claude/skills/ work the same and add frontmatter options

testObjectives.text: Structure iterative refinement workflows by providing concrete input-output examples, targeted feedback on specific failures, and batched issue descriptions for consolidated evaluation.
keyPoints: 2-3 input -> expected output pairs
Targeted feedback: which case, what expected, what came back
Batch interacting issues in one message; fix independent ones one at a time
Wrong: 'It's still wrong, try again'. Right: 'Case 3: input 12/05 should give 2026-05-12, got 2026-12-05.'

testObjectives.text: Determine when to use plan mode versus direct execution based on task scope, reversibility, architectural uncertainty, and the need for stakeholder review before implementation.
keyPoints: Scope: many files -> plan; one file -> direct
Reversibility: hard to undo (schema, migration, API contract) -> plan
Architectural uncertainty: several valid designs -> plan
Stakeholder review needed first -> plan

traps.wrong: Put team rules in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
Put a CLAUDE.md in every folder that has test files
Put a long workflow in CLAUDE.md
traps.why: CLAUDE.md is always loaded; wastes context

traps.wrong: Run the verbose analysis skill in the main context
Use plan mode for a one-line fix
traps.why: Plan mode adds no value for clear, small tasks

traps.wrong: Run claude "review" in CI
traps.why: Without -p the job waits for input

traps.wrong: Ask the same session to review its own code
Re-review from scratch on each commit
traps.right: Include prior findings; report only new/open

traps.wrong: Describe the format in more prose
Write 'always run Prettier' in CLAUDE.md
traps.why: CLAUDE.md is guidance; hooks are deterministic

domains.title: Prompt Engineering & Structured Output
domains.summary: How you write precise prompts, use few-shot examples, force structured output with tools and JSON schemas, build validation-retry loops, use the Message Batches API, and design multi-pass review.

taskStatements.title: System Prompts with Explicit Criteria
taskStatements.oneLine: Say exactly what to report and what to skip.
concept: Vague instructions like 'be conservative' or 'only report high-confidence findings' do NOT improve precision. Claude needs explicit criteria: which issue types to report and which to skip.
One category with many false positives makes users distrust ALL findings.
steps: List what to report: bugs, security issues, data loss risks.
List what to skip: minor style, locally accepted patterns.
Define severity levels with a concrete code example for each level.
Measure false positives per category.
Temporarily disable high-FP categories, improve their prompts, turn them back on.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Too many false positives' -> explicit categorical criteria + examples. Not 'be more careful', not 'raise the confidence threshold'.

taskStatements.title: Few-Shot Prompting
concept: Few-shot examples are the most effective way to get consistent output format and consistent judgment on ambiguous cases.
Use 2-4 targeted examples focused on AMBIGUOUS cases, not easy ones. Show the reasoning (why this action over a plausible alternative). Good examples let Claude generalize.
Extraction: examples cover varied structures (informal measurements, inline citations vs bibliographies). Code review: acceptable patterns vs real issues.
steps: Collect real cases where Claude was wrong or inconsistent.
Pick 2-4 that represent the ambiguity.
For each: input -> correct output -> short reasoning ('Chose X, not Y, because...').
Use the exact output format you want.
Test on new cases to confirm generalization.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Inconsistent format or judgment on edge cases' -> few-shot with reasoning. 'Rule must be followed 100%' -> NOT few-shot; use code enforcement (Domain 1).

taskStatements.title: Structured Output with Tool Use and JSON Schemas
taskStatements.oneLine: tool_use + JSON schema. Nullable fields. Enum + 'other'.
concept: Most reliable way to get schema-compliant JSON: define a tool whose input_schema is your JSON schema, then have Claude call it. This eliminates JSON SYNTAX errors.
A strict schema does NOT eliminate SEMANTIC errors (line items not matching total, value in wrong field). Validate those in code (see 4.4).

table.title: Schema design rules
rows: Make a field nullable/optional when the source may not contain it
Prevents fabrication to fill a required field
Captures values you did not predict
Claude can say it is not sure instead of guessing
Put format normalization rules in the prompt

steps: Define the tool: name, description, input_schema.
Mark fields that may be missing as nullable.
Add enums with 'other' and 'unclear' where needed.
Set tool_choice to force the tool (or 'any' for several schemas).
Read the tool_use block's input. Validate semantics in code.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Claude invents values for missing fields' -> nullable/optional. 'JSON sometimes invalid' -> tool_use with a schema, not 'please return JSON'.

taskStatements.title: Validation, Retry, and Feedback Loops
taskStatements.oneLine: Retry with the specific errors. Do not retry absent data.
concept: After extraction, validate in code. If validation fails, retry and append the SPECIFIC validation errors. Claude then corrects the exact problem.
Retries work for format/structure errors. Retries do NOT work when the information is absent from the source - return null or flag for review.

Self-correction fields: extract stated_total AND calculated_total (mismatch flags error); add conflict_detected boolean for inconsistent sources; add detected_pattern in review findings to analyze why developers dismiss findings.
steps: Run extraction.
Validate: types, required fields, sums, date formats.
If errors: send the SAME document + previous output + the specific errors ('line_items sum 450 != total 500').
Limit retries (e.g. 2).
If data does not exist in source: stop retrying; set null or route to human review.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Retry just resends the same prompt' -> wrong; include specific errors. 'Field keeps failing because it is not in the document' -> do NOT retry; make it nullable.

taskStatements.title: Batch Processing Strategies
taskStatements.oneLine: Batches API: 50% cheaper, up to 24 h, custom_id, no multi-turn tools.
concept: SLA calculation: a document can wait for the next submission window, then up to 24 h for the batch. So: window + 24 h <= SLA. Example: SLA 30 h -> window <= 6 h. The guide's example uses 4-hour windows for a safe margin.

table.title: Message Batches API
rows: Up to 24 hours. No guaranteed latency SLA
Each request has a custom_id; use it to match results to inputs
No multi-turn tool calling inside one request
Non-blocking, latency-tolerant: overnight reports, weekly audits, nightly test generation, large backlogs
Blocking work: pre-merge checks, live chat, anything a person waits for

steps: Refine the prompt on a small sample first (e.g. 50 docs) with synchronous calls.
Build the batch; give each request a unique custom_id (e.g. document ID).
Submit and poll until the batch ends.
Match results by custom_id.
Resubmit ONLY the failed items by custom_id with a fix (e.g. chunk documents that exceeded the context limit).
taskStatements.examTip: 'Pre-merge check must finish in minutes' -> synchronous API. 'Nightly job, cut cost' -> Batches. 'Need tool calls in the middle' -> NOT Batches.

taskStatements.title: Multi-Instance and Multi-Pass Review
concept: A model that generated content keeps its reasoning context and is less likely to question its own decisions. Self-review is weak.
An independent instance (new call without the generator's reasoning) beats self-review instructions or extended thinking.
steps: Pass 1: per-file local analysis (one call per file).
Pass 2: cross-file integration analysis (interfaces, data flow).
Pass 3: independent verification pass; each finding gets a confidence score.
Route by confidence: high -> post; low -> human review or drop.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Generator reviews its own output and misses errors' -> independent reviewer instance. Not 'ask it to review more carefully'.

testObjectives.text: Design extraction schemas with optional fields, nullable values, and appropriate enum definitions that allow the model to accurately represent missing or ambiguous information without fabricating values.
keyPoints: Required value + absent data = fabrication
Field may not exist -> nullable / not in required -> null
Fixed set -> enum; unexpected values -> 'other' + detail; ambiguous -> 'unclear'; exists-but-unstated -> 'not_stated'
Tell Claude in the field description to use null when absent
Distractors: 'do not hallucinate' prompt, make all fields required, retry until filled, remove the field

testObjectives.text: Apply extraction accuracy patterns - structured schemas with optional fields, format normalization instructions, and few-shot examples - to reduce hallucination and improve consistency across varied document formats.
keyPoints: Schema controls structure and blocks fabrication
Normalization rules: dates YYYY-MM-DD, amounts as numbers without symbols, units in kg
2-4 examples from DIFFERENT document formats, including one where a field is missing (output null)

testObjectives.text: Select and implement the most reliable structured output method - tool use with JSON schema, prompt-based formatting, or prefilled responses - based on required schema compliance strictness.
keyPoints: Prompt-based formatting: lowest reliability
Prefilled response (start turn with '{'): medium; format start fixed, schema not enforced
Tool use + JSON schema + forced tool_choice: highest
'Downstream parser breaks', 'must match schema' -> tool use + JSON schema

testObjectives.text: Implement tool use with defined JSON schemas to enforce structured output compliance, and configure tool_choice to guarantee tool invocation when conversational responses would cause downstream failures.
keyPoints: If Claude can reply 'Here is the data...' in text the parser fails
Set tool_choice any or the specific tool so a tool_use block always comes back

testObjectives.text: Design feedback loop mechanisms that capture structured metadata about model errors and use those patterns to improve prompts, schemas, or few-shot examples in future iterations.
keyPoints: Record per output: field, error type, detected_pattern, reviewer decision (accepted / dismissed + reason)
Aggregate to find most-failing / most-dismissed patterns
Fix the source: tighten prompt criteria, change schema, add few-shot
Re-measure on the same validation set

testObjectives.text: Select the appropriate API processing mode - synchronous Messages API or asynchronous Message Batches API - based on latency requirements, workflow blocking behavior, and acceptable processing windows.
keyPoints: Blocking or fast response -> synchronous
Non-blocking and up to 24 h acceptable -> Batches (50% cheaper)

traps.wrong: 'Be conservative, only high-confidence findings.'
traps.why: Vague words do not change precision

traps.wrong: Add 20 easy examples
traps.why: Quality and coverage of ambiguity matter

traps.wrong: 'Please output valid JSON' in the prompt
Strict schema guarantees correct data
traps.right: Schema fixes syntax; validate semantics in code
traps.why: Totals and field placement can still be wrong

traps.wrong: Make every field required
traps.right: Nullable fields for data that may be absent

traps.wrong: Retry until valid
traps.right: Retry with specific errors; stop if data is absent
traps.why: Absent data never appears by retrying

traps.wrong: Use Batches API for pre-merge checks to save cost
Resubmit the whole batch after some failures
Ask the generator to self-review with extended thinking

domains.title: Context Management & Reliability
domains.summary: How you keep critical facts in long conversations, when to escalate, how errors propagate in multi-agent systems, how to avoid context degradation, how to calibrate human review, and how to keep source provenance.

taskStatements.title: Context Window Management
taskStatements.oneLine: Case facts block. Trim tool output. Key facts at start.
concept: Progressive summarization risk: summaries turn exact values (amounts, dates) into vague text.
Lost in the middle: models handle the beginning and end of long input well; findings in the middle can be missed.
Tool result bloat: an order lookup can return 40+ fields when only 5 matter.
The API is stateless: you send the complete conversation history with each request.
steps: Extract transactional facts (order numbers, amounts, dates, status, promises) into a CASE FACTS block.
Include the block in every prompt, OUTSIDE the summarized history. Never summarize it.
Trim tool outputs to relevant fields before adding to history (a PostToolUse hook can do this).
When aggregating long inputs: key findings summary at the BEGINNING + explicit section headers.
Make subagents return structured data (key facts, citations, relevance scores), not verbose text.
taskStatements.examTip: 'After a long chat the agent forgot the exact refund amount' -> case facts block outside the summary. Not a bigger context window.

taskStatements.title: Escalation and Ambiguity Resolution
taskStatements.oneLine: Human request, policy gap, no progress. Not sentiment.
concept: Frustrated customer but issue is simple and in scope -> acknowledge frustration and offer the fix. If they repeat the request for a human -> escalate.
Multiple customer matches (two 'John Smith') -> ask for another identifier (email, order number). Do not pick by heuristic.

table.title: Escalation triggers
columns: NOT a valid trigger by itself
rows: Customer explicitly asks for a human -> escalate immediately
Policy is silent or ambiguous (e.g. competitor price match)

steps: Write explicit escalation criteria in the system prompt.
Add few-shot examples: escalate vs resolve, with reasoning.
For hard limits (refund > $500) also add a hook (Domain 1).
On escalation send a structured handoff (customer ID, root cause, amount, recommended action).
taskStatements.examTip: Sentiment analysis and confidence scores are DISTRACTORS for escalation. Correct triggers: human request, policy gap/exception, no progress.

taskStatements.title: Error Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems
taskStatements.oneLine: Structured error context. No silent failures.
concept: When a subagent fails, the coordinator needs structured error context: failure type, query attempted, partial results, possible alternatives.
Anti-pattern 1 - Silent suppression: returning an empty result as success (coordinator thinks 'no data exists').
Anti-pattern 2 - Workflow termination: stopping the whole workflow because one source failed.
steps: Subagent retries TRANSIENT errors locally.
If still failing: return a structured error (type, query, partial results, alternatives).
Coordinator decides: retry with another source, or continue with a gap.
Final report includes coverage annotations: which findings are well supported, which areas have gaps.
taskStatements.examTip: Generic status like 'search unavailable' hides context. Choose the answer that passes structured detail and continues with annotated gaps.

taskStatements.title: Codebase Exploration and Context Degradation
concept: In long sessions context degradation happens. Symptom: inconsistent answers and references to 'typical patterns' instead of the specific classes found earlier.

table.title: Techniques
rows: Claude writes key findings to a file; they survive context limits and compaction
Verbose exploration runs in a subagent; main agent keeps high-level coordination and summaries
Compresses the conversation to free context during long exploration
Each agent exports state to a known file; after a crash the coordinator loads the manifest and resumes

steps: Delegate wide searches to an Explore subagent; get a summary.
Record confirmed facts (class names, file paths, decisions) in a scratchpad file.
Use /compact when context grows large.
For long multi-agent jobs, export state to a manifest after each step.
On restart, load the manifest and continue.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Answers become generic after hours of exploration' -> context degradation. Fix with scratchpad + subagents + /compact. Not a bigger model.

taskStatements.title: Human Review and Confidence Calibration
taskStatements.oneLine: Stratified sampling. Accuracy per type and field.
concept: 97% overall accuracy can HIDE poor accuracy on one document type or field. Always measure by document type AND field.
Stratified random sampling: sample from each segment, including high-confidence results, to find hidden error patterns.
Field-level confidence scores must be CALIBRATED with a labeled validation set. Raw model confidence is not reliable.
Route low-confidence, ambiguous, or contradictory extractions to humans.
steps: Build a labeled validation set.
Measure accuracy per document type and per field.
Calibrate confidence thresholds against the labels.
Auto-accept only segments that meet the target.
Keep stratified random audits on auto-accepted results.
Send the rest to human review.
taskStatements.examTip: '97% overall, so automate everything' -> wrong. Check PER SEGMENT first.

taskStatements.title: Information Provenance and Multi-Source Synthesis
concept: Summaries can lose attribution. Each claim keeps a claim-source mapping: source URL, document name, excerpt, publication/collection date.
Two credible sources differ -> annotate the conflict with BOTH sources; do not pick one.
Different numbers may come from different dates -> require dates so a temporal difference is not treated as a contradiction.
Render content by type: financial data as tables, news as prose, technical findings as structured lists. Separate well-established from contested findings.
steps: Require every subagent to return claims with source metadata and dates.
Merge claims; keep mappings through every step.
Detect conflicts; check dates first.
Annotate real conflicts with both sources.
Label each finding established or contested.
taskStatements.examTip: 'Final report has no citations' -> sources were lost in summarization. Fix: structured claim-source mappings passed through the pipeline.

testObjectives.text: Apply context management strategies - subagent isolation, scratchpad files, and targeted file reading - to sustain coherent codebase exploration across sessions exceeding context limits.
keyPoints: Subagent isolation: wide exploration in a subagent, keep only the summary
Scratchpad (e.g. NOTES.md): write confirmed facts, read it at next session start
Targeted reading: Grep first, Read only relevant files/line ranges
Distractors: bigger context model, read all files at start, rely on --resume alone

testObjectives.text: Explain why conversation history must be explicitly included in each API request and identify the correct mechanism for maintaining state across multiple turns in a stateless API.
keyPoints: Messages API has no memory between calls
Each request contains the full messages array (user, assistant, tool_use, tool_result)
Your application stores and appends history
Summarize old turns but keep a case facts block

testObjectives.text: Apply escalation decision criteria to determine when an agent should immediately honor a human escalation request versus attempt autonomous resolution using available tools.
keyPoints: Explicit human request = escalate immediately, do not try to resolve first
Frustrated but no request and in scope = resolve, acknowledge frustration
Policy gap = escalate

testObjectives.text: Design human review routing strategies that direct extractions to reviewers based on confidence scores, document characteristics, and field-level ambiguity rather than random sampling.
keyPoints: Route by risk: low calibrated confidence, unusual/new document types, poor scans, ambiguous or conflicting fields
Random sampling is for AUDITING auto-accepted items, not choosing what humans review

traps.wrong: Increase context window size to keep facts
traps.why: Facts get lost in summaries, not only by size

traps.wrong: Escalate when sentiment is negative
traps.right: Escalate on human request, policy gap, no progress

traps.wrong: Escalate when Claude's confidence < 0.7
Pick the most recent account when names match
traps.why: Heuristic choice risks the wrong customer

traps.wrong: Return [] when a source fails
traps.right: Return structured error with partial results

traps.wrong: Abort the research when one source fails
Trust 97% overall accuracy
Choose the more credible statistic
traps.right: Annotate the conflict with both sources
